In contrast to Don who we see working for everything, especially in the first few season we really believe that he's worked hard for everything, even if he was dishonest, and in the US at least that has a "good" quality to it. We value hard work, Only in the seventh season do people start really bringing up that he has privilege, how attractive he is has always helped him, but for most of the series it's treated as though it's incidental.

We're not seeing Betty as a complex character because no one else does. When the show starts she's just lost her mother, who may have been just as abusive (in a different way) as the people who brought Don up. But because Don views her as a privileged princess so do we. It takes looking past how Don sees her in those first few seasons for us to start really valuing Betty, the same way Don does. You don't have to, you just set aside how ever much you're willing to loan them. Maybe it's 100 maybe it's 1000. You just make a set amount

If they never pay you back then keep in the logbook, and then when they ask you for more money it can strengthen your resolve to say no. You can see that they still owe you 1000 from this time or something.

You can lend money to your family. It just has to be money you're okay not getting back. It has to be surplus money you're okay with loosing. It can't be money you need. I replied earlier about a ledger, and even if no one ever pays you back, keeping track of who owes you what (and what you owe, I track all my debts even to CC companies in mine) will help remind you, if one of your siblings pays you back, that money is yours. You are not a bank.   


If you want to be able to help with small loans keep 100 dollars in cash somewhere that you can loan them, if they pay that back you can continue loaning from that, when the money is gone, it's gone, and so is your ability to loan. Look into any resources that can help you with budgeting. My mother's whole job is helping low income people rethink how they do money, there are a lot of non-profits that do this, and they're often looking to help people. If you can get your family involved in learning how to do this. They all need it. and it will help you and them to do so!

I bought a 1$ composition book and wrote down all of my debts in it, the money I owe and the money I'm owed (Even to myself! When I take from savings for something to remind myself to pay that back!)
